text:
Two teams on the skids meet at Madison Square Garden. The Kings lost 3-1 at New Jersey on Saturday, one of the Devils' three straight wins, and sit 2-3-0 in their last five. Alex Turcotte is out, while Quinton Byfield is day-to-day and could return. The Rangers are 1-3-1 in their last five after a 7-4 loss at Ottawa, where Drake Batherson scored three. Igor Shesterkin is on injured reserve, and Adam Fox plays his 500th NHL game.

Our numbers see little between them. At five on five, the Kings have taken 48% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and the Rangers 51%. The Kings are better than their record: a -11 goal difference against -3.6 expected, with finishing and goaltending costing them. Los Angeles also takes 4.3 penalties a game, which keeps handing out power plays, and New York's penalty kill allows just 0.52 expected goals a game. In net, projected starters Darcy Kuemper (-1.2 goals saved above expected, meaning saves beyond what the shots warranted) and Dylan Garand (+0.2) are both near even this season. Kuemper was at -6.8 last year, while Garand was at +3.9 in three games. Our model has the Rangers at 3.11 expected goals tonight and the Kings at 2.88.

Watch Artemi Panarin against his old team, at 70% for a point, and Alexis Lafrenière, who is 61% and carrying a point-per-game pace, as Adam Herman of Bleacher Report posted. Pavel Dorofeyev is 34% to score. Our under-the-radar pick is Alex Laferriere, at 53% for a point, with his ice time projected up to 20:31.
